nodes.name: Hourly Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 1 h. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Read Pending Queue (HubSpot)
nodes.notes: Looks up an existing HubSpot contact by last-modified date — finds records the pipeline hasn't processed yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Work in Batches
nodes.notes: Loop controller — releases 20 item(s) per pass. Output 2 (loop) processes the batch, output 1 (done) fires after the last batch. Watch out: Output 2 is the loop body, output 1 fires once after the last batch. Wiring these backwards is the classic mistake.

nodes.name: Process Batch Item
nodes.notes: POST https://api.example.com/v1/leads — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Respect Rate Limits
nodes.notes: Pauses 2 seconds — spacing calls to respect rate limits. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Aggregate Batch Results
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Mark Completed in MySQL
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Augment contact records: HubSpot, batched

**Pattern:** Data Enrichment · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers outreach work end to end across HubSpot and MySQL.

It moves through 8 working steps, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Read Pending Queue (HubSpot)
3. Work in Batches
4. Process Batch Item
5. Respect Rate Limits
6. Aggregate Batch Results
7. Mark Completed in MySQL
8. Tag Pipeline Metadata

## Why it exists

Doing outreach work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Read Pending Queue (HubSpot) → Work in Batches → Process Batch Item → Respect Rate Limits → Aggregate Batch Results → Mark Completed in MySQL → Tag Pipeline Metadata

## Use it for

- Teams keeping HubSpot and MySQL aligned by hand for outreach
- Outreach sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before HubSpot
- A backlog too large to push into HubSpot in one pass, across 8 nodes
- Outreach work where "Read Pending Queue (HubSpot)" is still a manual step before HubSpot

## You get

- Keeps HubSpot and MySQL in step for outreach, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed HubSpot or MySQL call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 8 nodes in this outreach build
- The pause before HubSpot is durable — a outreach run survives a restart
- Batches the work so HubSpot rate limits never break a outreach run
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 8 nodes for outreach before wiring HubSpot

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; HubSpot private-app token; MySQL connection.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The batch size and the Wait between iterations exist specifically to respect the downstream API's rate limit — processing everything as fast as possible just gets the workflow throttled or banned. Marking items completed only after a batch succeeds leaves a clean resume point if the run dies mid-way, instead of an ambiguous half-processed state.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Lower the batch size and raise the wait — measure the throughput/reliability tradeoff directly.
2. Simulate a failed item mid-batch and see exactly what 'Mark Completed' captures.
3. Point the queue read at a different store platform.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**The loop runs forever or exits immediately**
Cause: The loop output and the done output are wired the wrong way round.
Fix: Output 2 is the loop body; output 1 fires after the last batch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your outreach process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- MySQL: grant the user only the tables this workflow touches; avoid `GRANT ALL` on the schema.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
outreach payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
